description: We are Guardians of the Galaxy
summary: MARS: OUTPOST ZERO is a browser-based educational simulation where players manage a Mars outpost for 30 Sols (Martian days). You balance four life-support resources — power, water, food and oxygen — respond to crises like solar storms and equipment failures, and make decisions that have both immediate and delayed consequences. After every run, a full debrief shows your decision timeline, the leadership traits your choices revealed, and lessons linked directly to real NASA and ESA resources on life support, radiation, redundancy and risk management. The game is free to play in any browser with no login required, making space science accessible to anyone. It was built to show that the engineering problems NASA engineers face every day — resource scarcity, cascading failures, decision-making under uncertainty — can be understood and felt through play.
details:
What it does and how it works: Players run a Mars outpost for 30 Sols. Each Sol they pick one action — from routine operations and resource allocation to multi-Sol projects like repairing the generator or planting crops — and end the day. A deterministic simulation engine applies production, consumption, radiation exposure and any delayed effects from earlier decisions, then checks whether a new crisis event fires. Three consecutive Sols without power end the mission. The game has eight occupations (Engineer, Botanist, Geologist, Chemist, Pilot, Commander, Scientist, Medical Officer), three mission sites (Lunar, Mars, Deep-Space), over 50 crisis events across five story chapters, and a full debrief that traces every consequence back to the choice that caused it.

Benefits and intended impact: The debrief links each lesson to real NASA and ESA pages — ECLSS, the Apollo 13 mission, ISS water recovery, Mars 2020 rover communications, radiation shielding and more. Players finish a run with an intuitive understanding of why these engineering principles matter, grounded in actual mission history. The game is fully accessible in a browser, requires no installation, and works as a guest with no account.

Tools and languages used: React 18, TypeScript (strict mode), Vite 5, Tailwind CSS 3, Vitest (35 test files), browser localStorage for persistence, Node.js and FFmpeg for the How to Play video, and Vercel for hosting. Code was developed with AI coding assistance (Kiro). Chapter and ending artwork was AI-generated and is labelled with a visible watermark throughout the game and in the How to Play video.

Creative choices: The simulation engine is fully deterministic — the same decisions always produce the same outcome — which makes the debrief trustworthy as a learning tool. Every resource number on screen is derived from the engine's own daily calculation, so the dashboard never does its own maths. The five-chapter storyline unfolds through fixed Sol events, giving the run a narrative arc even when played purely as a strategy game.
